label: copy-phase input f (fed-back f), from the 2nd recalled token on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input token is f, meaning the model just output f and that f is fed back in. Over 99.9% of activation mass is on in_tok == f. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on any other copy-phase input token. It is weak or silent when the f is fed back at recall_idx 1 (original position 0). Magnitude rises with recall_idx: firing rate goes from about 2% at recall_idx 2 to a plateau around 3% from recall_idx 4 on. It is also larger when L is longer. The strongest activations come on the first fed-back f near the end of the sequence, and a second f right after it fires more weakly. The remaining false positives are mostly f inputs at early recall positions (recall_idx 2-3) that do not fire.

issues: Main claims hold. On test: P 0.877, R 0.985, F1 0.927, mass recall 0.996. Dropping the recall_idx condition (copy phase & in_tok==f) gives mass recall 1.0. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases (0 of about 3.7M steps). Other copy-phase input tokens account for only about 24 activations in total (0:16, d:4, h:2, c:1, e:1).

The '2% to 3% plateau' numbers are overall firing rates per step, not rates on f inputs, so they understate how selective the feature is. The fraction of copy-phase f inputs that fire is about 0.68 at recall_idx 2, 0.83 at recall_idx 3, 0.98 at recall_idx 5 and 0.99 at recall_idx 6 and above. At recall_idx 1 it is about 0.006.

The false positives are not a clean category. They are activations below threshold on f inputs at early recall_idx, with short L (precision 0.56 at L<=5) or many outputs still to go (precision 0.50 at to_go>=4). There is also a little dependence on the previous token (precision 0.41 after g, 0.51 after 0, at recall_idx 2). The explanation already acknowledges early-position weakness.

One magnitude pattern the explanation leaves out: the top activations are almost all the first f of an 'f f' pair in the original sequence, i.e. the step whose output is also f. At recall_idx 2 the share of f inputs that fire rises to 0.97 when out_tok == f. The 'second f fires more weakly' claim is consistent with this.

Alternative predicates did not beat the original on test: recall_idx>=3 gives F1 0.867, adding (recall_idx==2 & out_tok==f) gives 0.872, and gating by L gives 0.908. The original stays the best at 0.927.
